title: Hempholm source-module overview
summary: Hempholm is a rural hemp-growing village used as the crisis site for an adventure about a magical grotesque tree, visible local danger, premature celebration, and deeper root-creature retaliation.
must_not_claim: Hempholm was encountered before C1S4 in prior-only mode
source geography is Elderwyld canon

title: Hempholm hemp economy
summary: The source module presents Hempholm as a village specializing in durable, strong hemp cultivation. This supports hemp-themed merchants, trade talk, local pride, and road-hook rumors.
must_not_claim: Torvak is from the PDF source
exact Elderwyld trade routes are known

title: Road hook merchant role
summary: The source module includes formal hooks and a merchant rumor structure; the Longmont adaptation can replace that with Torvak Hempdealer, a memorable road merchant who left Hempholm quickly and points the party toward the crisis.
must_not_claim: Torvak is source-module canon
Torvak is observed play in prior-plus-support unless C1S4 recap is allowed

source_reference.document: User adaptation note + Of Conks & Cons hook structure

title: Grotesque tree as visible threat
summary: The source tree is an obvious village-scale problem: sickly, tough-looking, thorned, magical, with shiny metallic leaves and a tendency to attack creatures that come too close.
must_not_claim: tree swatted Karsemine unless C1S4 oracle is allowed
exact campaign stats are known

title: Tree mechanics and investigation clues
summary: The tree can be investigated through visible metallic leaves, magical aura, root-network implications, danger radius, retaliation, and fire vulnerability/risk.
must_not_claim: specific C1S4 initiative sequence
tree grows exactly ten feet unless sourced

source_reference.section: Area 5 / Advancing the Story / Appendix A

title: Torbin and Jove family pressure
summary: The source module centers the tree in the Jove family garden. Torbin is the boy who planted the magical conk; his father Mark Jove is angry, frightened, and worried about survival, harvest, damage, and winter.
must_not_claim: Longmont C1 prior-only context knows Torbin/Jove
exact table portrayal before C1S4 oracle is allowed

title: Morwin and the village store
summary: Morwin Blackwell runs Hempholm's dusty general store, sells basic goods and hemp products, and can provide local gossip or friction with other merchants.
must_not_claim: Morwin appeared in observed C1S4 unless recap/adaptation says so

title: Saladin as optional magical merchant
summary: Saladin is an elderly elven mage/trader with a magical wagon and unbidden thoughts. He can be used as optional weird-color NPC, source of magical context, or recurring traveler.
must_not_claim: Saladin is present in Longmont C1 unless intentionally adapted

title: Narfi as optional wounded healer
summary: Narfi Granitetooth is a grieving dwarven priest in the Shacks who can become a healer or social challenge if approached with mercy and faith.
must_not_claim: Narfi is campaign canon unless introduced

title: Villagers attempt reckless action
summary: The source module includes escalation where villagers become fed up, drink, take axes, and try to attack the tree. The tree mauls them, turning social pressure into injuries and a healing problem.
must_not_claim: exact Longmont mob sequence unless observed C1S4 is allowed

title: Small problems around Hempholm
summary: The module includes side hooks such as repairing a distillery, cutting mistaken gemstones, and a food/drink competition. These support tool proficiencies and village texture.
must_not_claim: these side problems occurred unless introduced

title: Premature celebration after visible victory
summary: After the tree is destroyed, the source villagers celebrate with food, ale, spirits, stories, children, and lowered guard. This is designed to make the coming attack more threatening.
must_not_claim: specific C1S4 celebration events or Steve unless sourced

title: Caretakers as second-wave horror
summary: The source module reveals that the destroyed surface tree had root-like caretakers below. They emerge hours later during celebration or firefighting to attack villagers and structures.
must_not_claim: root-like beetles are observed C1S4 facts in prior-only mode
exact number/tactics are campaign canon unless adapted

title: Descent into hollow roots
summary: The module can continue underground through holes torn in the village into warm hollow roots that feel more like stone or metal than wood.
must_not_claim: the party descended in C1S4
root tunnels are confirmed campaign canon before observed play or adaptation

title: The Marrow, guardian, helix, and child
summary: At the root network's center, the source module reveals a chamber with a wooden helix, glowing sack, guardian, metal resin, and a strange child-like being. This supports moral-choice and future-consequence prep.
must_not_claim: this reveal exists in the Longmont campaign unless deliberately adapted

source_reference.section: The Marrow / Fate of the Child

title: Metallic and root-material treasure
summary: The source module provides precious metal leaves, metal resin, and valuable root/caretaker material as loot or crafting hooks after the tree/root threats are defeated.
must_not_claim: Bonogo's exact blacksmith trade unless C1S4 oracle is allowed

source_reference.section: Area 5 / The Marrow / Rampage of the Caretakers

title: Mages' guild cleanup continuation hook
summary: The source module can continue with a guild agent seeking to erase evidence, compensate witnesses, gather information, and pursue the strange child or adventurers.
must_not_claim: Baldur's Gate mages' guild exists in Elderwyld unless adapted
Paelias exists in campaign canon unless introduced
